content.text: This explains what data SparkStream handles, where it lives, and what control you have over it. It is written to be read, not to be skimmed past. SparkStream is built on two principles that shape every feature: earn your trust, and hold the bare minimum personal data needed to run the service.
The short version

items: Almost everything lives on your own computer. The server only gets involved for features that genuinely need it.
Your Twitch login token never leaves your machine, and is stored encrypted by your operating system.
Sensitive data we do store on the server (billing email, support messages, security logs) is encrypted at rest.
Direct messages are end to end encrypted. SparkStream cannot read them, and staff will never message you.
Payments go through Stripe. SparkStream never sees or stores your card details.
We never sell or share your data, and there are no advertising or tracking cookies anywhere in the app.
You can export or delete your data at any time.

content.text: Who runs SparkStream, and who is responsible for your data

SparkStream is operated by SparkStream App Ltd, a private limited company registered in England and Wales, United Kingdom, company number 17328916, registered office 128 City Road, London, United Kingdom, EC1V 2NX. SparkStream App Ltd is the data controller for your personal data, which means it is responsible for deciding how and why your data is used. The cloud parts of the service run on managed hosting. You can contact us about your data, or anything else in this policy, by email at hello@sparkstreamapp.com, or through the Direct Support page in this app, where you will reach a real person.
What stays only on your computer

Everything that can be local, is. Your reward mappings, stream event triggers, game profiles, community goals, activity log, live feed history, notification preferences, accessibility settings, and integration settings (such as your OBS WebSocket details and Discord webhook URLs) are stored on your machine using your operating system's standard application storage. Your live feed history is the recent follows, subs, gifts, cheers and raids your dashboard shows, and it includes the viewer names Twitch sends with them. It is kept to the most recent 50, held separately for each channel you sign in with, and you can clear it whenever you like from the History view. Your TTS provider keys, including any ElevenLabs key, also stay local. None of this is transmitted to the SparkStream server.
Your Twitch connection

When you connect Twitch, SparkStream stores your access token locally using OS level encryption. It is used only to talk to Twitch directly from your machine: to watch for channel point redemptions and stream events, and to manage rewards you created through SparkStream. The token is never sent to the SparkStream server. SparkStream only requests the permissions its features need, and you can revoke access at any time from your Twitch account security settings.
What the SparkStream server stores, and only when you use the feature
The server holds the least it can to make each cloud feature work. If you do not use a feature, there is nothing stored for it. Here is the full list, by feature:

items: Account: your Twitch user ID and public Twitch username (not your real name), and the dates you first and last signed in. This is how the service knows you exist.

Pro and billing: your subscription status, your Stripe customer and subscription references, your Pro credit balance and a history of credit changes, and a billing email only if you provide one (stored encrypted). Stripe processes the payment itself; SparkStream never receives your card number.
Referrals: if you use a referral code, a record linking the referred account to the referring account, so the reward can be applied once.
Community Hub: the content you post to the Community Hub, such as feature requests, forum posts and replies, poll responses, and bug reports, tied to your username.
Support tickets: the category, status, and the subject and message text of tickets you open. Subject and message content are encrypted at rest.
Direct messages: your public key, plus message content that is end to end encrypted. The server only ever holds ciphertext it cannot read.
Analytics (Pro): redemption events for your own channel. The viewer identity attached to each event is hashed and encrypted, never stored in readable form.
Mobile approvals (Pro): a short lived queue entry while a redemption waits for approval on your phone. These auto expire after a few hours.
Security log: a limited record of security relevant events, such as failed sign in attempts. Any IP address is stored encrypted and kept only for a short period.
Forum reports: if you report a forum post, the report itself (which post, the reason, and any details you add, encrypted at rest). Reports are visible only to the moderation team.

Signed-in devices: a coarse device name (like SparkStream Desktop on Windows) and when each device first signed in and was last active. This powers the Active devices list in Settings and new sign-in email alerts. No IP addresses or hardware identifiers.

Account lock: if you use the lock button in a new sign-in email, the fact and time of that lock, kept until you or support unlock it. The link in that email is stored only as a hash, so it cannot be read back out of the database.

Support PIN: if you set one, the 4-digit code, stored encrypted. It exists only to answer match or no match when you verify your identity to support, and it is never displayed to anyone, staff included, after you set it.

content.text: Encryption

Sensitive fields on the server (billing email, support ticket content, security log IP addresses, and the viewer identity in analytics) are encrypted at rest. Direct messages go further: they are end to end encrypted, so only the intended recipient's device can decrypt them. SparkStream staff cannot read your direct messages, and SparkStream will never contact you through the direct message feature. Anyone claiming to be SparkStream staff in your DMs is not.
Payments

Pro subscriptions are handled by Stripe. SparkStream stores only the references Stripe gives us, your subscription status, and an optional billing email. Your card details are entered with Stripe and are never seen or stored by SparkStream.
Third parties we rely on

items: Twitch, for authentication and the channel point and stream event data the app reacts to.
Stripe, for processing Pro payments.
ElevenLabs, only if you choose to add a key for AI voices. Your usage is billed by ElevenLabs, not SparkStream.
Discord, only if you set up a webhook for the Discord Message action.
A transactional email provider, used to send account related emails such as a receipt or an access change notice.
Managed cloud hosting, where the server and its database run.

content.text: There are no advertising networks, no analytics trackers, and no tracking cookies anywhere in SparkStream. We do not sell or share your data with anyone for marketing.
Where your data is processed

SparkStream is based in the United Kingdom, but some of the companies we rely on are based elsewhere, mostly the United States. This means a limited amount of your data, such as the payment information handled by Stripe and the data held on our managed hosting, is processed outside the UK. Whenever data leaves the UK, we rely on the safeguards UK law recognises: where a provider is certified under the UK extension to the EU-US Data Privacy Framework, known as the UK-US Data Bridge, we rely on that certification; otherwise we rely on the ICO's International Data Transfer Agreement or Standard Contractual Clauses. The protections in this policy apply to your data wherever it is handled.
Our lawful basis for using your data
UK data protection law requires us to have a lawful basis for using your personal data. Depending on the data, ours are:

items: Performing our contract with you. Most of what we do exists only to provide the service you signed up for, such as running your Pro subscription, your Community Hub activity, and your support tickets.
Our legitimate interests. We keep the service secure, prevent fraud and abuse, and run the community safely. We only rely on this where it does not override your own rights and freedoms.
Complying with a legal obligation. We keep certain records the law requires us to keep, such as transaction records for tax.
Your consent. For anything genuinely optional, such as providing a billing email. You can withdraw consent at any time by stopping use of that feature.

content.text: What SparkStream will never do

items: Sell, rent, or monetise your data or your viewers data.
Store viewer chat, redemption input, or stream event content on the server beyond what a feature you switched on actually needs.
Build behavioural profiles on you or your viewers.
Collect data just in case it might be useful later.
Read your direct messages, or contact your viewers pretending to be you or SparkStream.
Use dark patterns to hide what is collected or how to remove it.

content.text: Your rights and controls

items: Disconnect Twitch and wipe your local data from inside the app at any time.
Export a copy of the data the server holds about you, from your Profile, as a readable file.
Ask for your server side data to be deleted by opening a support ticket. We will do it, no questions asked, beyond anything we are legally required to keep.
Choose what you use. Most data only exists because you used the feature that creates it.
You also have the rights UK data protection law gives you, including to access, correct, or erase your data, and to object to or restrict certain uses. Ask through support and we will help.

If you are in the United Kingdom and unhappy with how we handle your data, you have the right to complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) at ico.org.uk. We would appreciate the chance to put things right first, so please consider contacting us before you do.

content.text: Data retention

We keep data while your account is active and for as long as the feature it belongs to needs it. When you ask for deletion, we remove your data, with one narrow exception: records we are legally required to keep. In practice this means the billing and payment records needed under UK tax law, which requires companies to retain financial records for six years for HMRC. These are limited to the transaction records held through Stripe, are kept separate from your ordinary account and usage data, are used only to meet that legal obligation, and are deleted once the retention period ends. Short lived data, such as the mobile approval queue and security logs, expires automatically.
Children and younger users

You must be at least 16 to hold a SparkStream account, or older if the law where you live sets a higher minimum. SparkStream is not intended for children under this age, and we do not knowingly collect their personal data. If you believe a child under 16 has given us personal data, contact us and we will remove it. We also build in protections that help keep younger users, and everyone, safer: you choose whether to use direct messages at all, you can limit who is allowed to message you, including to your channel moderators only, or turn messaging off entirely, and screen content protection is on by default. Reporting tools and staff moderation back these up across the Community Hub.
Changes to this policy
If this policy changes in a meaningful way, you will be told clearly inside the app. Changes are never made quietly or buried in an unrelated update.

How this policy can change is governed by the Sovereign User Promise, which forms part of our agreement with you. No material change to how we collect or use your data takes effect until 14 days after we send you notice, and throughout that time you can download your data, delete your historic data, or delete your account. If anything in this policy conflicts with the Promise, the Promise applies, and any change to this policy that would weaken it is itself a material change under the Promise. You can read the Promise in full at sparkstreamapp.com/trust.

This is a commitment, not fine print. If anything here is unclear, or you want to know exactly what is held about your account, open a support ticket and ask. The effective date and app version for this policy are shown at the top of this document.

These terms are the agreement between you and SparkStream App Ltd, which we refer to here as SparkStream, for using the app and its services. To be upfront about who you are agreeing with: SparkStream App Ltd is a private limited company registered in England and Wales, company number 17328916, registered office 128 City Road, London, United Kingdom, EC1V 2NX. These terms are written in plain language on purpose. By using SparkStream you agree to them, so please read them. They work alongside the Privacy & Data Policy, which is part of this agreement.
1. Who can use SparkStream

You need to be at least 16, or older if the law where you live sets a higher minimum, and you need the authority to accept these terms. If you are using SparkStream on behalf of an organisation, you confirm you can agree on its behalf.
2. What SparkStream is

SparkStream is a desktop app that connects to your Twitch account and runs actions in response to channel point redemptions and stream events. The core app runs on your own computer. Some features, mostly Pro ones, use the SparkStream server to provide cloud functionality such as analytics, mobile approvals, the Community Hub, support tickets, and direct messages.
3. Your account and your Twitch connection

SparkStream connects to Twitch using OAuth, and only asks for the permissions its features need. You are responsible for your own Twitch account and for keeping your access to it secure. You can revoke SparkStream's access at any time from your Twitch security settings, which will stop the cloud features from working until you reconnect.
4. Acceptable use

Use SparkStream lawfully and in line with Twitch's own Terms of Service. You are responsible for the actions you set up, including scripts, programs, HTTP requests, and hotkeys that run on your machine. Do not use SparkStream to harass, harm, deceive, or defraud anyone. Do not attempt to break, overload, probe, or abuse the SparkStream server or its services, and do not try to access data that is not yours.
5. Community Hub and conduct

The Community Hub is a shared space. Keep it civil and constructive. SparkStream staff may moderate, edit, or remove content, and may restrict or remove your access to community features, for conduct that breaks these terms or harms others. If you believe a moderation decision was wrong, you can appeal by opening a support ticket.
6. Direct messages

Direct messages are end to end encrypted between users. SparkStream cannot read them, and SparkStream staff will never message you through the feature. Treat anyone in your DMs claiming to be SparkStream as an impersonator. You can report a message for review, which shares that message and the five before it, for context, with staff. You see exactly what will be sent before you send it, and nothing else in the conversation is shared. To comply with our legal safety obligations, reported messages will be reviewed for illegal content or abuse. Using direct messages to harass, scam, or abuse others can result in your messaging access being removed.
7. Pro, credits, and billing

Pro features need an active Pro subscription, which is billed through Stripe. Pro access runs on a credit system where one credit is one day of Pro. Your subscription tops up credits, and credits drain by one per day, which gives you a grace period if a payment is late. Pro is tied to your Twitch account and is not transferable. Bonus credits from referrals or loyalty are a thank you, not a cash equivalent, and cannot be exchanged for money. You can cancel any time through the billing portal. Fees already paid are non refundable except where the law requires otherwise. If prices or what Pro includes change, you will be told in advance.
8. Chargebacks and payment disputes

If you have a billing problem or want a refund, contact support first. Most issues are sorted out quickly. Starting a chargeback or payment dispute with your bank or card provider may result in your Pro access and account being temporarily suspended pending investigation. If a dispute is found to be fraudulent or made in bad faith, we may immediately end your account, remove any remaining credits including referral and loyalty bonuses, and decline to offer Pro to that account or payment method in the future. We reserve the right to challenge disputes we believe are not legitimate, including by sharing records of your use of the service with the payment provider. None of this affects any refund rights the law gives you.
9. Referral program

Your referral code is your Twitch username. Referral rewards are granted only when a genuinely new user subscribes to Pro for the first time using your code. You may not refer yourself, create fake or automated accounts, or otherwise game the program. SparkStream may withhold or reverse referral rewards, and may remove access to the program, where it sees abuse.
10. Third party services

SparkStream works with Twitch, Stripe, and optionally ElevenLabs and Discord. Your use of those services is also governed by their own terms, and any costs they charge, such as ElevenLabs voice usage, are yours to pay. SparkStream is not responsible for outages or changes in third party services.
11. Intellectual property

SparkStream, including its name, design, and original content and features, belongs to SparkStream App Ltd. You may not copy, modify, redistribute, or reverse engineer the app except where the law expressly allows it.
12. No warranty

SparkStream is provided as is. We work hard to make it reliable, but we cannot promise it will be error free, always available, or compatible with every system. You are responsible for what the actions you configure do on your machine and your stream.
13. Limitation of liability
Nothing in these terms excludes or limits our liability for death or personal injury caused by our negligence, fraud, or any other liability that cannot be excluded by English law.

Our responsibility for app defects: if a bug or defect in the core SparkStream software damages your device or your digital content, and that damage was caused by our failure to use reasonable care and skill, we accept our legal responsibility to either repair the damage or pay you appropriate compensation. This strictly applies to our core code and does not cover damage caused by user-configured scripts, third-party hardware, or external webhooks.

Physical and third-party hardware disclaimer: SparkStream is digital automation software. We accept no liability for damage, data loss, or harm caused by user-configured scripts, third-party mappings, or arbitrary code executed through the SparkStream environment. If you configure the app to interact with physical hardware, smart home devices, or IoT appliances, you do so entirely at your own risk. We have no control over, and accept no responsibility for, the safety, functionality, or defects of any third-party hardware. You are solely responsible for ensuring that any physical devices you connect have their own adequate safety safeguards and are operated in a safe environment.

To the maximum extent the law allows otherwise, SparkStream's total liability for any claim arising from your use of the app is limited to what you paid for your current billing period, or 10 pounds, whichever is greater. SparkStream is not liable for indirect, incidental, or consequential losses.
14. Suspension and termination

You can stop using SparkStream and cancel Pro at any time. We may suspend or end your access if you break these terms. When your account ends, your Pro access stops and your server side data is deleted, except anything we are legally required to keep, as described in the Privacy & Data Policy.
15. Changes to these terms

If these terms change in a meaningful way, you will be shown the updated version in the app and asked to agree before continuing. Changes are never applied silently, and the date of the latest version is always shown.

Some changes also affect how we handle your data. The Sovereign User Promise forms part of these terms, and where a change is a material change under it, that Promise applies as well as this section: we send notice in the app and by email, the change does not take effect for 14 days, and throughout that time you can download your data, delete your historic data, or delete your account. If anything in these terms conflicts with the Promise, the Promise applies, and any change to these terms that would weaken it is itself a material change under the Promise. You can read the Promise in full at sparkstreamapp.com/trust.

These terms are governed by the laws of England and Wales, and any dispute falls under the courts of England and Wales.
